messages.subject: Diagnosing causes of errors?
parts:
Hi team,

Im running the same model on 4 datasets (that are all laid out in the same way...they are actually all generated from a single master file):

TPm1 = gng_m1(data=dataTpress, niter=2000, nwarmup=1000, nchain=4, ncore=4)
TLm1 = gng_m1(data=dataTlift, niter=2000, nwarmup=1000, nchain=4, ncore=4)
SPm1 = gng_m1(data=dataSpress, niter=2000, nwarmup=1000, nchain=4, ncore=4)
SLm1 = gng_m1(data=dataSlift, niter=2000, nwarmup=1000, nchain=4, ncore=4)

The top three work, but I cant fit the fourth model (SLm1  which results in this error:

Error in new_CppObject_xp(fields$.module, fields$.pointer, ...) : 
  Exception: model24ac77dc185a_gng_m1_namespace::model24ac77dc185a_gng_m1: pressed[i_0__][i_1__] is 13, but must be less than or equal to 1  (in 'model24ac77dc185a_gng_m1' at line 8)

I guess this might be due to some funky behaviour from at least one participant in the fourth dataset, but it really isnt obvious eyeballing the data. So two questions:

1) Do you know what the error is referring to?
2) If not, is there an easy way for me to debug this issue? I.e. is it possible for me to see "'model24ac77dc185a_gng_m1' at line 8" so I can try to reverse engineer it?

Thanks so much!

Oli

Best,
Young

messages.subject: Re: Diagnosing causes of errors?
parts:
I found two trials with 13 and 92 in the 'keyPressed' column (the column name should be 'keyPressed' intead of 'KeyPressed' - maybe it doesn't matter in the latest version?). I found them with these commands:


tmp = read.table("SL.txt", header = T)
table(tmp$KeyPressed)


If I remove those two trials, it runs fine! 

Best,
Young

See attached.

messages.subject: Re: Diagnosing causes of errors?
parts:
Also, just FYI—you can take a look at the stan files directly on the github page, when can be useful for finding out what is going on: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/master/commons/stan_files/gng_m1.stan

Here, Stan expects that the `pressed` array will only contain 0/1 values, and so the 13/92 values caused the error (see line 8).

Best,
Nate
